headline: Organic growth accelerates; GAAP margins stay pressured

drivers.explanation: Reported growth of 2.2% trails organic growth of 9.5% mainly due to an 8.3% net drag from the September 2025 Purification and Filtration divestiture, partly offset by the Acera acquisition.
Growth reflects strong performance across all segments, driven by volume and product mix, including advance orders placed ahead of ERP cutovers.
GAAP and adjusted gross margin both increased, driven by an IEEPA tariff refund.
GAAP operating income margin decreased primarily due to net legal costs plus separation and restructuring costs.
Net income growth of 2.2% roughly tracks the rise in pretax income, tempered by a higher effective tax rate (14.4% vs. 12.5% a year ago).
Adjusted EPS growth outpaced GAAP as adjusted operating margin expanded to 28.4% from 21.9%, per the non-GAAP reconciliation table, on a lighter net normalization burden.
Free cash flow came in ahead of expectations, driven by timing of tax payments and insurance proceeds.
H1 cash fell $475M as $355M of treasury-stock purchases and $164M of investing outflows outweighed a $38M net operating cash inflow.

Management cites "strong execution" ahead of expectations; the quarter's headline event was the announced intent to separate the Health Information Systems segment as part of its transformation strategy.

summary_short: Solventum's Q2 2026 revenue rose 2.2% to $2,209M (+9.5% organic), with adjusted diluted EPS up 50.9% to $2.55 while GAAP diluted EPS grew 3.9% to $0.53; the company also raised its full-year 2026 guidance for organic sales growth, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow.
summary_long: Revenue of $2,209M grew 2.2% reported / 9.5% organic, with the gap explained by the Purification and Filtration divestiture. Gross margin expanded on an IEEPA tariff refund, but GAAP operating income fell 15.4% y/y on separation, restructuring, and litigation costs; adjusted operating margin still rose to 28.4%. Adjusted diluted EPS climbed 50.9% to $2.55; GAAP diluted EPS rose 3.9% to $0.53. Free cash flow of $144M beat expectations on tax-payment timing and insurance proceeds. Cash fell to $403M (-28.2% q/q) after $355M of H1 buybacks, while long-term debt eased to $4,573M. Solventum announced intent to separate its Health Information Systems segment and raised FY2026 guidance for organic sales growth (+2.5% to +3.0%), adjusted EPS ($7.10-$7.20), and free cash flow ($200M-$300M).
